title: CoreWeave results lift tech as Nvidia rebounds after two-day slide
dek: Stock futures pointed higher on Veterans Day, led by the Nasdaq, after CoreWeave's strong quarter eased worries about AI spending and Nvidia bounced. The bond market is closed, so Tuesday's 5% 10-year yield and near-certain December rate-hike bets carry over untouched.
quick: Nasdaq 100 futures were up roughly 1.5% to 1.9% before the open and S&P 500 futures about 0.7% to 0.9%; Dow futures were only slightly higher.
CoreWeave jumped about 13% to 17% premarket after beating forecasts, raising its 2026 revenue outlook and reporting a backlog of about $133 billion.
Nvidia rebounded roughly 3% to 5% premarket after two days of losses tied to the investigation of CEO Jensen Huang.
The U.S. bond market is closed for Veterans Day. The 10-year yield stands at 5.00% from Tuesday, and futures price a December Fed hike as very likely.
Oil edged up, with Brent near $92, after tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz dented hopes for a quick end to the Iran conflict.
Stocks trade normal hours today, but there is no major U.S. data and no Fed speakers. Thursday and Friday bring jobless claims, a 30-year bond auction, PPI and a dozen Fed talks.

blocks.head: CoreWeave's quarter revives the AI trade
blocks.what: CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of about $3.66 billion after Tuesday's close, up roughly 168% from a year earlier, according to the company's release and coverage by CNBC and the WSJ. It raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion and said its backlog of contracted business reached about $133 billion, up from about $104 billion in June. MarketWatch and CNBC said management expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments, and the company said it would lean on prepayments and secured, draw-as-needed credit lines rather than unsecured bonds. The shares rose about 13% to 17% premarket, per Investing.com, CNBC and TradingKey.
blocks.why: CoreWeave has become a stand-in for worries that the AI data-center buildout is running on too much debt. A clean quarter and a less bond-dependent funding plan eased those worries, lifting chip and AI infrastructure stocks in the U.S., Europe and Asia and putting the Nasdaq ahead of the Dow.
blocks.watch: Whether the rally holds through the session, given the pressure from 5% yields. CoreWeave still posted a net loss of about $709 million, per the company release.

blocks.head: Nvidia bounces after two bruising days
blocks.what: Nvidia shares rose roughly 3% to 5% in premarket trading, according to Investing.com and TradingKey, after two days of losses that the Globe and Mail said erased about $430 billion in market value. The stock fell after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. officials have linked to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead an internal investigation, per the WSJ, NYT and CNBC.
blocks.why: Nvidia is one of the largest weights in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, so its bounce alone adds meaningfully to index gains. Chip peers such as AMD and Micron were up around 6% premarket, per TradingKey, though MarketWatch noted it is unclear whether Nvidia's troubles will shift actual customer orders to rivals.
blocks.watch: Any update from the investigation, the board or Washington. The House China committee chair told CNBC he expects answers.

blocks.head: Rate-hike bets stay locked in, with no bond trading today
blocks.what: Tuesday's October CPI report showed prices up 0.4% for the month and core prices up 0.3%, both above forecasts, per CNBC and other outlets. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he leans toward a quarter-point hike in December and that a half-point move should be considered if core inflation runs around 0.3% or higher, according to several reports of his remarks. The 10-year Treasury yield ended Tuesday at 5.00% and the 2-year at 4.75%. U.S. bond markets are closed today for Veterans Day, as SIFMA recommends.
blocks.why: Higher yields make borrowing costlier and raise the bar for stock valuations, especially for tech and small companies. With cash Treasurys closed, there is no fresh reading on rates today, so stocks are trading on company news while the rate backdrop stays where Tuesday left it.
blocks.watch: Thursday's 30-year bond auction and Friday's producer price index are the next tests for yields.

blocks.head: Oil firms as Hormuz tanker attacks dent peace hopes
blocks.what: Brent crude is near $92 a barrel and WTI near $86, both slightly higher, after falling to two-month lows on Tuesday. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported a tanker was struck off Oman, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on what it called an unauthorized route, according to Anadolu and other outlets. The American Petroleum Institute reported a 9 million-barrel rise in U.S. crude stockpiles last week, per market reports.
blocks.why: Oil remains a direct input to inflation. Prices that stay below October's highs above $110 help the inflation outlook, but renewed shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz would push energy prices, and possibly rate-hike odds, higher.
blocks.watch: The government's EIA inventory report comes Thursday, a day late because of the holiday.

blocks.head: TSMC will buy into Anthropic's IPO and OpenAI
blocks.what: TSMC's board approved buying up to $500 million of Anthropic shares at the IPO price and up to $500 million of OpenAI preferred stock, according to a TSMC filing with the SEC that the WSJ also reported. The board also approved about $40.9 billion in capital spending and a quarterly dividend of NT$9 a share. Anthropic, which set a range of $70 to $78 a share, has opened a retail offering in Australia and plans to begin trading on the Nasdaq Nov. 19, per CNBC.
blocks.why: Big strategic buyers lining up for the Anthropic deal signal demand for what could be one of the largest IPOs on record. A strong debut would support AI-related stocks, while a weak one could add to doubts about AI valuations.
blocks.watch: More anchor-investor announcements and any change to the price range before pricing.

blocks.text: Asia

Asian stocks mostly rose as chip and AI shares rallied, even after Wall Street's Tuesday decline, according to the AP. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained about 1.3% to 61,248.59, and South Korea's Kospi jumped about 2.6%, helped by chipmakers. China's Shanghai Composite rose about 0.5%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng was the exception, falling roughly 0.8%. The WSJ reported Asian government bond yields rose as markets priced in a Fed hike next month. CNBC reported Alibaba plans to list its AI chip unit, T-Head, in Hong Kong.
Europe

European shares are higher and the Stoxx 600 is again approaching its record high. Investing.com and other outlets had the Stoxx 600 up about 0.4% around midday, with Germany's DAX up about 0.9%, France's CAC 40 up about 0.7% and Britain's FTSE 100 up about 0.8%. Chip equipment makers such as ASML and BE Semiconductor gained after CoreWeave's results. It is a busy day for European earnings, with Siemens Energy, E.ON, RWE, ABN Amro and Vestas among the companies reporting, per XTB. In the UK, the WSJ reported an economic think tank argued the Bank of England should raise its key rate toward 5%.
Currencies

Currency moves are small after Tuesday's big dollar rally. The dollar index is near 102.3, up less than 0.1%. The euro is about $1.116 and the pound about $1.334, both little changed. The dollar is near 158.8 yen. China's yuan is steady around 6.67 per dollar.

Futures point to a tech-led rebound after Tuesday's losses, when the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,520.93, the Nasdaq dropped 0.7% and the Dow lost 0.3%. Reports through the morning had Nasdaq 100 futures up about 1.5% to 1.9% and S&P 500 futures up about 0.7% to 0.9%, while Dow futures were up only about 0.1% to 0.2%. The gap shows the bounce is concentrated in chips and AI names, which carry more weight in the Nasdaq. The Dow has fewer of them.

The VIX volatility index ended Tuesday near 19.5, a moderate level that suggests caution rather than alarm. CNBC reported investors had been rotating toward defensive sectors in recent sessions. Today's tech bounce tests whether that shift continues. Small caps, measured by the Russell 2000, fell 0.7% Tuesday. They are especially sensitive to rates and may lag while yields sit near 5%.

No Treasury cash trading today, so Tuesday's levels stand. The 2-year yield ended at about 4.75%, up about 20 basis points on the day. The 10-year ended at 5.00%, up about 14, and the 30-year at about 5.36%, up about 10. The short end rose most because it tracks Fed expectations most closely, which flattened the curve. The gap between the 10-year and the 2-year is now about 25 basis points.

Fed funds futures now treat a December hike as very likely. Reports citing CME FedWatch put the odds of a hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting anywhere from about 85% to 100% after the CPI report, depending on when the reading was taken, with a quarter-point move seen as the base case and a half-point move a minority bet of roughly 10% to 15%. Waller set out a bar for the larger move. Other officials have been less specific, so this week's speeches will show how widely his view is shared. Not everyone agrees: a portfolio manager quoted by MarketWatch argued the Fed should not hike again.
Fed speakers

items: Thursday: Hammack (8:30 a.m.), Barr (10:00 a.m.), Goolsbee (11:15 a.m.), Daly (1:10 p.m.), Schmid (1:30 p.m.) and New York Fed President Williams (6:30 p.m.).
Friday: Collins, Logan, Bowman, Daly and Jefferson.

blocks.text: Tuesday's sectors

Technology was the clear laggard on Tuesday, with the sector fund (XLK) down about 1.2% as Nvidia slid and higher yields hit high-valuation growth stocks. Industrials, materials, utilities and real estate also slipped slightly. Utilities and real estate often trade like bonds and tend to struggle when yields rise.

Financials led, up about 0.5%. Banks can earn more on loans when rates rise. Energy gained about 0.4%, communication services about 0.4% and health care about 0.3%. That mix of financials, energy and health care in front matches the defensive tilt CNBC described. Today's premarket action points to a reversal, with tech in front.
Premarket movers

items: CoreWeave: up about 13% to 17% after beating revenue forecasts, raising guidance and outlining a funding plan built on customer prepayments (CNBC, MarketWatch, Investing.com).
Nvidia: up roughly 3% to 5% as it tries to recover from two days of losses over the CEO investigation (Investing.com, TradingKey).
AMD and Micron: each up around 6% in the broad chip rebound, per TradingKey. Storage makers Sandisk and Seagate and chip designer Marvell were also higher, per Blockonomi.
Children's Place: filed for bankruptcy with about $881 million in debt, per MarketWatch.

blocks.text: Oil

Brent is near $92 and WTI near $86, both up less than 1%, after Tuesday's drop to two-month lows. The push and pull is between hopes for an end to the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, which pulled prices down from levels above $110 at the end of October, and new attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, which raise the risk of supply disruption. A large rise in U.S. crude stockpiles reported by the API is a counterweight. The consensus forecast for Thursday's EIA report is a small draw.
Gold

Gold futures are near $4,070 an ounce, up about 1%, partly recovering from Tuesday's drop of roughly 2% to 2.7%, per Invezz and FXStreet. Gold pays no interest, so it lost appeal when yields and the dollar jumped after CPI. Today's steadier dollar is giving it some room.
Crypto

Bitcoin is near $73,800 and Ether near $2,060, both slightly higher. CoinDesk reported Bitcoin dipped to about $72,700 on Tuesday, its weakest since Aug. 20, and analysts noted it had slipped below its 200-day moving average, a level many traders watch for trend direction. Crypto has been trading in step with tech stocks and rate expectations, so a firmer Nasdaq is helping at the margin.

items: No major U.S. economic data today. The calendar lists Veterans Day as a bank holiday, and banks and the Fed's payment systems are closed, so some transfers may settle Thursday.
Stocks trade normal hours (9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. ET), and stock-index futures settle normally, per CME.
The U.S. bond market is fully closed, per SIFMA's recommendation, so there will be no new Treasury yield readings until Thursday.
No Fed speakers are scheduled. Thursday's weekly oil inventory report from the EIA is pushed back a day.

rows: Whether a premarket jump of about 13% to 17% holds, and how investors read its shift to prepayments and secured credit lines instead of unsecured bonds.
IT services demand and whether AI tools are helping or hurting consulting revenue.
User growth and cash burn. The options market implies a large move, per TipRanks.
First report since the Vylor spin-off. Investors want standalone guidance to replace the pre-split $3.60 to $3.80 operating EPS range, per 24/7 Wall St.
First results as an independent company after the Corteva split.
Royalty income with gold near $4,000. Analysts have cut estimates over the past month, per 24/7 Wall St. and Benzinga.
Flight-simulator and pilot-training demand from airlines and defense customers.
Government consulting work and any effect from shifts in federal spending.

blocks.text: This list comes from earnings calendars at Kiplinger, TipRanks, Investing.com and StockTitan, because the app's own earnings feed did not load this morning. Calendars disagree on a few timings, so check before acting on any single name.

The week's second half is packed. Thursday brings weekly jobless claims (forecast 194,000, from 189,000), existing home sales (forecast 3.89 million), the delayed EIA oil report and a 30-year bond auction that will show whether buyers step in with long-term yields near 5.4%. Six Fed officials speak that day, ending with New York Fed President John Williams in the evening. As vice chair of the Fed's rate-setting committee, his view carries extra weight. Friday's producer price index (headline forecast 0.4%, core 0.3%) is the last big inflation reading before the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting decision, and five more Fed officials speak. Anthropic's IPO marketing continues ahead of its planned Nov. 19 debut, and news from the Nvidia investigation could move the market's largest stock at any time.

bottom_line: The tone is a cautious tech rebound. CoreWeave's results and Nvidia's bounce are lifting AI stocks, but with the 10-year at 5% and a December Fed hike largely priced in, the rate backdrop that drove Tuesday's selloff has not changed.
